1. First, I'll calculate total revenue per English product category for each year (2017 and 2018), filtering out canceled/unavailable orders.

args.purpose: Calculate total revenue per English product category for 2017 and 2018, excluding canceled/unavailable orders
args.sql:
SELECT 
    ct.product_category_name_english,
    EXTRACT(YEAR FROM o.order_purchase_timestamp) AS year,
    SUM(oi.price) AS total_revenue
FROM orders o
JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
JOIN category_translation ct ON p.product_category_name = ct.product_category_name
WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
  AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM o.order_purchase_timestamp) IN (2017, 2018)
GROUP BY ct.product_category_name_english, year
ORDER BY year, total_revenue DESC

args.purpose: Find categories in top 10 for both 2017 and 2018
args.sql:
WITH top10_2017 AS (
    SELECT ct.product_category_name_english
    FROM orders o
    JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id

    JOIN category_translation ct ON p.product_category_name = ct.product_category_name
    WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')

    GROUP BY ct.product_category_name_english
    ORDER BY SUM(oi.price) DESC

),
top10_2018 AS (
    SELECT ct.product_category_name_english

    JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id

)
SELECT t1.product_category_name_english,

FROM top10_2017 t1

    SUM(oi.price) AS total_revenue
FROM orders o
JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id
JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
JOIN category_translation ct ON p.product_category_name = ct.product_category_name
WHERE o.order_status NOT IN ('canceled', 'unavailable')
  AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM o.order_purchase_timestamp) = 2018
GROUP BY ct.product_category_name_english
ORDER BY total_revenue DESC
LIMIT 10
